title: Passing off vs trademark infringement - the difference that matters
p1:
Two businesses can fight over the same brand name… but the legal reasons behind the fight may be completely different.

Many people think passing off and trademark infringement are the same thing. They are not.
p2:
The surprising part? A business can win a passing off claim even without owning a registered trademark.

Passing off protects the reputation you have built in the market. It stops others from creating confusion and making customers believe their product is connected to yours.

Trademark infringement, on the other hand, usually comes into play when someone uses a registered trademark without permission.
p3:
Think of it this way: trademark infringement protects your registered legal right, while passing off protects the goodwill and trust customers associate with your brand.

For founders and businesses, this difference matters because registration is powerful, but reputation also has legal value. Building a brand is not just about owning a name—it is about owning the confidence people place in it.
conclusion: If a competitor copied your brand name but your trademark was not registered, do you think you should still have a legal remedy? Share your view.
